Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 69, verses 9–12:

{9–10} That is: likewise, apart from these two rebellious peoples, ʿAd and Thamud, there came others from the arrogant tyrants, such as Pharaoh of Egypt, to whom Allah sent His servant and messenger Musa ibn ʿImran, upon him be prayers and peace. He showed them the clear signs by which they became certain of the truth, but they denied and disbelieved out of wrongdoing and arrogance. And there came before him the deniers, and "the overturned cities" (al-mu'tafikat), that is, the towns of the people of Lut. All of them came "with the sin" (al-khati'ah), that is, with the act of transgression, which is disbelief, denial, wrongdoing, obstinacy, and whatever is joined to that of various kinds of disobedience and wickedness. "And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord": this is a generic noun; that is, each of these people denied the messenger whom Allah sent to them. So Allah seized them all "with a severe seizing" (akhdhatan rabiyah), that is, one exceeding the limit and measure by which their destruction is brought about.

{11–12} Among these peoples were the people of Nuh. Allah drowned them in the flood when the water rose over the face of the earth and overtopped its high places. Allah bestowed His favour upon the creatures who came after them, in that He carried them "in the flowing ship" (al-jariyah), which is the ark, while they were in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers, those whom Allah saved. So praise Allah and give thanks to the One who saved you when He destroyed the tyrants, and take heed from His signs which point to His oneness. For this reason He said: "that We might make it" (li-naj'alaha), that is, the ship, and what is meant is its kind, "a reminder for you" (tadhkirah), reminding you of the first ship that was built and its story, and how Allah saved upon it those who believed in Him and followed His messenger, and destroyed all the people of the earth. Indeed, the kind of a thing reminds one of its origin. And His saying: "and that a retaining ear might retain it" (wa-ta'iyaha udhunun wa'iyah), that is, those of understanding will comprehend it, know its purpose and its lesson. This is in contrast to those who turn away and are heedless, and the dull-witted and lacking in understanding, for they gain no benefit from the signs of Allah, because they do not retain the remembrance of Allah and do not reflect upon His signs.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 69, verses 25–37:

{25–29} These are the people of wretchedness. They are given their books, containing their evil deeds, in their left hands, as a distinction, a humiliation, a disgrace and an exposure. One of them will say, out of distress, grief and sorrow: ﴿Oh, I wish I had not been given my record﴾, because it announces entry into the Fire and everlasting loss. ﴿And had not known my reckoning﴾; that is, I wish I had been a forgotten thing, neither resurrected nor brought to account. For this reason he says: ﴿Oh, I wish it had been the end﴾; that is, I wish my death had been the final death after which there is no resurrection.

Then he turns to his wealth and his authority, and finds them to be a burden upon him. He did not send anything of them ahead for his Hereafter, and they will not benefit him even if he ransomed himself with them from the punishment. So he says: ﴿My wealth has not availed me﴾; that is, it did not benefit me in this world, since I did not send any of it forward, nor in the Hereafter, for the time of its benefit has passed. ﴿My authority has gone from me﴾; that is, it has departed and perished. Neither the armies, nor the multitude, nor the number, nor the equipment, nor the broad standing availed him. Rather, all of that was scattered like dust before the winds, the trade and the profits that came through it were lost, and in their place came worries, griefs and sorrows.

{30–37} Then it will be commanded concerning him to be punished, and it will be said to the harsh, mighty guardians (of Hell): ﴿Seize him and shackle him﴾; that is, put a collar around his neck that will choke him. ﴿Then burn him in the Blaze﴾; that is, turn him over in its embers and flames. ﴿Then, in a chain whose length is seventy cubits﴾: from the chains of Hell, which are extremely hot. ﴿Then thread him﴾; that is, run him through it, by having it enter his anus and exit his mouth, and he is suspended therein, and he will not cease to be punished with this terrible punishment. How evil is this punishment and retribution, and alas for him, for the reproach and rebuke! The cause that brought him to this place is that ﴿he did not believe in God, the Mighty﴾, being an unbeliever in his Lord, opposing His messengers and rejecting the truth they brought. ﴿And did not urge the feeding of the poor﴾; that is, there was no mercy in his heart by which he would show compassion to the needy and the poor, so he did not feed them from his wealth nor urge others to feed them, because of the absence of restraint in his heart. This is because the basis and foundation of happiness rest upon two matters: sincerity toward God, whose root is faith in God, and goodness toward creation in all its forms, the greatest of which is relieving the urgent need of the needy by feeding them what sustains them. These people had neither sincerity nor goodness, and therefore they deserved what they deserved. ﴿So there is no friend for him here today﴾; that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿no intimate friend﴾, that is, no relative or friend who would intercede for him to be saved from God's punishment or to attain His reward. ﴿Nor is intercession of any benefit with Him, except for one whom He has permitted﴾, ﴿the wrongdoers have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who is obeyed﴾. He has no ﴿food except from ghislin﴾: which is the pus of the people of the Fire, extremely hot and bitter, foul in smell and repulsive in taste. None eat this vile food ﴿except the sinners﴾, who strayed from the straight path and followed every road that leads to Hell, and therefore deserved the painful punishment.
